samples.label: Outdoor explorer
samples.comment: Maine takes the top spot for its rugged Acadia coastline and inland wilderness, followed by Tennessee for the Great Smoky Mountains; Pennsylvania offers decent Appalachian hiking, but Illinois and New Jersey focus too heavily on urban and city-centric attractions that don't align with my love for the outdoors.

samples.label: City and culture traveler
samples.comment: My preferences lean heavily toward major metropolitan hubs with world-class architecture, theater, and museum scenes; Chicago (IL) is a perfect fit, and Philadelphia/Pittsburgh (PA) offer excellent cultural depth. Tennessee (TN) is next for the rich musical history, followed by New Jersey (NJ) for its urban proximity and dining, while Maine (ME) ranks last as I prioritize city culture over nature-focused landscapes.

samples.label: Beach and relaxation traveler
samples.comment: New Jersey takes the top spot for its Atlantic beaches and boardwalks, which are perfect for my love of relaxation. Maine follows for its beautiful ocean scenery, though the water is a bit chilly for my preference. Illinois, Pennsylvania, and Tennessee rank lower because they lack the warm, swimmable beach atmosphere I prioritize in a vacation.

samples.label: Food and music traveler
samples.comment: Tennessee captures the heart of my interests with its legendary music history and barbecue traditions, followed by Illinois for Chicago’s world-class jazz and blues clubs and diverse culinary scene. Maine offers a unique regional food culture with its lobster traditions and coastal character. New Jersey and Pennsylvania follow, as they offer interesting pockets of culture, but they don't quite match the specific music and food-centric depth I prioritize for a first-time trip.

samples.label: History enthusiast
samples.comment: Pennsylvania is my top choice because Philadelphia is arguably the most significant city for American history, and I would spend a full week exploring its historic districts and museums. Illinois follows for the world-class architecture and art scene in Chicago. Tennessee is third because of the rich musical history in Memphis and Nashville, which I find fascinating. New Jersey offers interesting historic sites, though it ranks below the others for my specific interests. Maine is last; while beautiful, it is less focused on the historic and civil rights themes I prioritize for a one-week trip.

samples.label: Family vacation planner
samples.comment: Tennessee is my top pick because the mix of Great Smoky Mountains hiking and the kid-friendly music history in Nashville and Memphis creates a perfect educational yet fun balance. New Jersey ranks second for the classic boardwalks and beaches, which are a staple for school-age kids. Pennsylvania follows with a great variety of history and outdoor recreation. Illinois is next, as Chicago is fantastic, but it feels more urban-heavy for a full week. Maine is last; while beautiful, it is a bit more wilderness-focused than what I usually look for with two children.
